post.summary: Create a snapshot of dependencies for a repository
post.desc:
Create a new snapshot of a repository's dependencies.

The authenticated user must have access to the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

params.name: owner
params.desc: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

params.name: repo
params.desc: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

application/json.title: snapshot
application/json.description: Create a new snapshot of a repository's dependencies.

version.description: The version of the repository snapshot submission.

id.description: The external ID of the job.

correlator.description: Correlator provides a key that is used to group snapshots submitted over time. Only the "latest" submitted snapshot for a given combination of `job.correlator` and `detector.name` will be considered when calculating a repository's current dependencies. Correlator should be as unique as it takes to distinguish all detection runs for a given "wave" of CI workflow you run. If you're using GitHub Actions, a good default value for this could be the environment variables GITHUB_WORKFLOW and GITHUB_JOB concatenated together. If you're using a build matrix, then you'll also need to add additional key(s) to distinguish between each submission inside a matrix variation.

sha.description: The commit SHA associated with this dependency snapshot. Maximum length: 40 characters.

ref.description: The repository branch that triggered this snapshot.

detector.description: A description of the detector used.

name.description: The name of the detector used.

version.description: The version of the detector used.

url.description: The url of the detector used.
